source_publication.title: AI Data Security: Best Practices for Securing Data Used to Train & Operate AI Systems

ADS002.text: During collection and processing, consider data minimization as a potential data-security focus area.
ADS002.type_reason: Data minimization governs collection and processing, matching 3.2 responsible data acquisition/use; it is not a policy governing who may use AI systems (3.3).
ADS002.no_link_reason: A potential data-minimization focus is supported, but the table supplies neither the personal-data conditions of Sensitive Data Entered nor a concrete attack/exfiltration condition. Avoid inventing the intervening exposure scenario.
ADS002.review: Source and classification reviewed; no blocking questions.
ADS002.human_review: Should privacy-preserving data-use controls without an identified personal-information harm or adversarial mechanism remain without a risk target? Retain no-supported-target for this document. Types remain supported; no control is discarded.

ADS020.object: Sensitive AI training and development data
ADS020.text: Implement anonymization or depersonalization techniques to keep sensitive attributes confidential. When possible, use data masking for AI training and development, replacing sensitive data with inauthentic but realistic information retaining dataset value distributions. Practical implementation of privacy techniques may be limited by computational cost.

links.reason: Replacing sensitive information with realistic inauthentic values and anonymizing sensitive attributes directly aims to keep those attributes confidential, including the source’s PII example. It remains conditional on feasibility and says nothing about a realized disclosure.

ADS020.type_reason: Masking/anonymizing data is responsible data curation and privacy protection, directly within 3.2. It does not establish provenance for AI-generated content (2.4).
ADS020.review: Source and classification reviewed; no blocking questions.

ADS021.text: When appropriate and possible, differential privacy is a privacy-preserving option using a prespecified privacy budget to govern noise added to data, with tradeoffs between protection against membership inference and target-task accuracy. Practical implementation may be limited by computational cost.

links.reason: When appropriate and possible, budgeted noise is intended to reduce membership-inference exploitation of training data. Use the broad security parent because the exact Inference Attack leaf states attribute inference, whereas this source specifically names membership.

The source expressly states a privacy-versus-target-task-accuracy tradeoff: the same protection can lower accuracy, a prospective adverse effect matching insufficient intended-task accuracy. It does not assert an observed performance failure.

ADS021.type_reason: Primary 2.3: the budgeted-noise method is an explicit technical safeguard against exploiting training-data membership. Additional 3.2: the prescribed privacy budget governs privacy-protecting data use. Neither label asserts adoption, model-value alignment or proven effectiveness.
ADS021.review: Source and classification reviewed; no blocking questions.
ADS021.human_review: Does the prototype Inference Attack definition’s “attribute information” include training-data membership inference? The present mapping uses the unambiguous security parent and preserves the separate accuracy trade-off. No risk-link field is unfinished.

ADS028.actor: Foundation model developers/providers and, for filtering attestations, data curators
ADS028.object: Foundation-model training data, sources and filtering
ADS028.text: When a consumer ingests a foundation model trained by another party, its developers need to be able to provide assurances about training data and sources and certify that no known compromised training data was included. Ideally, curators and providers should attest to filtering methods and provide evidence such as test results.

links.reason: Provider capability to furnish attestations and evidence enables consumers to assess compromised-data risks in external foundation models. Consumer vetting/acceptance is the intermediate activity; attestation alone is not prevention.

ADS028.type_reason: Provider assurances, certifications and ideally filtering-test evidence communicate risk-control claims and evaluations to consumers, matching risk disclosure in 4.2 rather than technical prevention.
ADS028.review: Source and classification reviewed; no blocking questions.

ADS030.text: Before using third-party datasets or foundation models, data consumers should strongly consider requiring formal certification from providers that their systems contain no known compromised data, and exercise caution about models lacking assurances.

links.reason: Strongly considering a formal cleanliness certificate supports safer third-party acceptance only if providers can substantiate the certificate and consumers use it in acceptance decisions. That assurance/verification step is explicit in the surrounding provider and acceptance guidance; requesting a certificate alone cannot remove compromised data.

ADS030.type_reason: A prospective provider-certification requirement before acquiring datasets/models is a data acquisition governance condition in 3.2. It does not constitute an external audit (3.1) or provider disclosure already performed (4.2).
ADS030.review: Source and classification reviewed; no blocking questions.

ADS033.actor: Data consumers downloading curated web-scale datasets
ADS033.object: Downloaded items from curated web-scale datasets
ADS033.text: Consumers downloading curated web-scale datasets should check hashes at download to detect changes and discard data that fails the check.

links.reason: Consumers directly exclude changed downloaded content by discarding hash failures before use, constraining split-view poisoning of referenced datasets.

The download-time hash check discards changed items that fail verification, directly blocking that poisoned-data acquisition route into training use. The Data Ingest parent explicitly describes a pathway; its mitigation does not require redesigning the AI’s ingestion capability.

ADS033.type_reason: Hash verification with discard is an integrity/authentication admission safeguard under 2.1.
ADS033.review: Source and classification reviewed; no blocking questions.

ADS063.object: Operational AI models and their input/output data
ADS063.exceptions: Slow/gradual versus abrupt changes are likelihood indicators, not definitive diagnoses.
ADS063.text: Monitor model accuracy, performance, inputs and outputs and regularly check associated data for updates at intervals appropriate to the system and application. Use meaningful statistics to compare expected metrics and training-versus-test distributions. Gradual changes suggest drift while abrupt dramatic changes suggest compromise; in high-stakes applications continuous performance monitoring plus direct input analysis is important before impacts occur. The gradual/abrupt distinction is a likelihood indicator, not a definitive diagnosis.

links.reason: Statistical comparisons of training/test distributions and operational inputs/performance assess distribution shift. Check intervals are application-dependent, with more continuous direct analysis in high-stakes cases.

Abrupt/dimensional changes in performance/input data are indicators used to distinguish possible poisoning from gradual drift. The source says more likely, so this is probabilistic observation rather than a definitive diagnosis or prevention.
Checking accuracy, performance and expected outputs directly assesses whether the model performs its intended task reliably, independent of whether a deviation is drift or malicious.

ADS063.type_reason: Continuous/regular monitoring of operational model performance and input/output distributions is post-deployment monitoring under 3.5.
ADS063.review: Source and classification reviewed; no blocking questions.
